t: as it says, "and you shall slaughter," etc.. And zevichah (slaughter) is a synonym for shechitah.
and it says regarding a firstborn with a blemish. In the law of the firstborn of a pure animal that has a blemish, which is given to the kohanim and eaten as ordinary meat (Hilchot Bechorot 1:3).
thus you learn that a wild animal is like a domesticated animal, etc.. In this verse the wild animals, the tzvi and the ayal, were equated with domesticated pure animals.
and the laws of shechitah are the same for all of them. The laws are identical for all kinds of wild animals, domesticated animals and birds.
as long as it is twitching. As long as it moves its limbs after the slaughter, since it has not yet died completely.

and it is included in "you shall not eat over the blood". But there is no prohibition here of a limb from a living animal for a Jew, since it has already been slaughtered (see Hilchot Melachim 9:12-13).
and he does not receive lashes. Since many prohibitions are learned from this verse, the prohibition is a 'general negative commandment' for which one is not lashed (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 18:2-3).
and he salts it well and rinses it well. In order to remove its blood, which is forbidden to eat (Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 6:10, 6:12).
as I commanded you. Meaning: as I told you. And because the details are not found explicitly in Scripture, it is understood that they were explained orally.
as we explained at the beginning of this work. Introduction to the Mishneh Torah, 1.
the neck. And there the windpipe and the gullet are cut (below 5:9).
from the beginning of the place where, when it is cut, it contracts. The cavity of the gullet contracts and closes, but above this place the gullet remains open.
to the place where it becomes hairy and starts to be ridged like the rumen. Near the rumen.
,. The gullet is not smooth on the inside but is lined with hard hair-like projections, similar to the inner side of the rumen.
in the windpipe. The trachea.
from the hat-like rim. At the upper part of the windpipe there is a piece of cartilage that looks like a hat (the epiglottis).
the wing of the lung. The upper lobes of the lung, which look like wings and are spread out at the sides of the lung.
when the animal stretches its neck to graze. For then the windpipe is stretched and extends a bit more out of the chest cavity.
the animal forced itself, etc.. It compelled itself and stretched its neck.
that the slaughterer forced the simanim. He stretched the windpipe and gullet from their place.

and slaughtered at the place of slaughter in the neck, etc.. The slaughter was in the neck, in the place where it is normally fitting to slaughter, but because of the pulling the simanim were cut in a place not fit for slaughter.
doubtful neveilah. As the law of any animal about whose valid slaughter there is doubt (below 3:18). 9. In the middle of the neck. At the front of the neck.
and the second half. Exactly half, and not the majority of the siman.
a windpipe that was half cut. That was cut earlier, and such a cut does not disqualify the animal (see below 3:19).
whether he began to slaughter in the whole place... his slaughter is valid. For in the end the cutting of the majority of the windpipe was completed by an act of slaughter.
to check the simanim. Whether the majority of them was cut.
for every animal in its lifetime is forbidden, etc.. And therefore one must make sure that the slaughter was done properly.
with a flint. A sharp stone.
with a reed membrane. The hard outer layer of the reed, which they sharpened, and which can serve as a knife.
like a furrow. A groove.
from one direction. That is felt only in one direction of the knife's movement, as explained in the next halachah.
a knife that is checked by pushing forward. When the slaughterer moves the knife on his fingernail away from himself (see below halachah 23).
by pulling back. When he brings it toward himself.
rising and falling like a snake. Its blade is not straight but goes up and down.

like the touch of the tip of an ear of grain that clings to the finger. The blade is rough like the bristles at the tip of grain stalks, and when tested the finger catches on it and does not slide over it.
one who tears out a reed or a tooth. From where they grow.
or who cut off a flint. He cut it from the rock.
slaughtered with them while they are attached from the beginning of their creation... his slaughter is invalid. For one slaughters only with a detached object.
the jaw of an animal that has teeth in it. A jawbone with the teeth set in it.
because they are like a sickle. Which is serrated.
and even though it is fixed in it. And this is not considered slaughtering with an attached object. 22. If he heated the knife in fire and slaughtered with it. While it was still glowing.
his slaughter is valid. And there is no concern that the simanim were burned and scorched before he cut them.
one side of which is serrated like a sickle. The back of the knife is nicked and serrated like a sickle.
and its other side is smooth. Even.
and on this side and that side. On both sides of the blade.
its edge. The tip of the knife.
lest it was nicked on the skin. For there is concern that the knife was nicked on the skin of the neck, before cutting the simanim.
he must check between each one and each one. And so he will ensure that each of them was slaughtered properly.

for the presumption is that the knife was nicked by a hard thing that he broke with it. We assume that the nick was caused by breaking bones, and not that it was nicked on the skin before the slaughter.
any butcher who did not check his knife with which he slaughters before a sage. A slaughterer who did not show the knife to a sage, to verify that it is indeed smooth as it should be.

we excommunicate him, etc.. They impose a ban on him for acting improperly, in a matter that could lead to a mishap. For the details of the ban see Hilchot Talmud Torah 7:2-4 (and there 6:14 is a list of all who are banned).
we remove him. We dismiss him from his position.
terefah. In this context: forbidden to eat.
the length of the knife. The length of the blade.
the scalpel. A knife with a small blade.
liable with his life. On the Sabbath, to stoning, and on Yom Kippur, to karet.
the Temple court. Of the Temple.
sacrificial items of the altar. What was consecrated to the altar.
for meat of desire. In a case where a person desires to eat meat without bringing it to the Temple as an offering.

"If the place which the Lord will choose is too far from you". And the verse continues: "then you shall slaughter from your herd and from your flock... as I commanded you, and you may eat in your gates, according to all the desire of your soul."
in all the gates. The places of settlement.
the meat is pure. And it does not become impure as neveilah
(. Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTum'ah 1:2).
and its ashes are forbidden. Like all that is buried (see Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashin 19:11-13).
even if he slaughtered for healing, etc.. Even when he slaughtered in the Temple court not for the purpose of eating, it is considered slaughter and it is forbidden.
but one who wrings the neck in the Temple court... are permitted for benefit. For all of these ways are not considered slaughter at all.
one who wrings the neck. Kills in a way other than slaughter.
one who uproots. He uprooted the windpipe or gullet from where they are attached and thereby killed the animal (see below 3:14).
a gentile who slaughtered. And his slaughter is invalid (below 4:11).
all non-sacred food. Foods that are not sacred (see also Hilchot Bikkurim 4:4).
words of tradition. The tradition of the Sages.
one who says, "this animal is a peace offering and its offspring is non-sacred". In this case only the mother becomes sanctified and not the fetus (see Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 15:1).

and its offspring is permitted to eat. Although the slaughter of the mother permits the fetus to be eaten (Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 5:14), it is not considered non-sacred food slaughtered in the Temple court.
to the image. A reflection.
murky. That are not clear.
a slaughterer... goes down into the pit. Since it is evident that he intends to keep clean and not to serve idolatry.
and in the marketplace he should not do so, lest he imitate the minim. It is forbidden to do so in public places and openly, for that is the way of the minim, the heretics.
stretches the neck. So that the simanim do not shift during the slaughter.
moves the knife back and forth. On the neck.
whether it was lying down. Lying down, and he slaughtered it from above.
lest the animal come down with its body weight and be cut without a forward and back motion. That the animal's weight will cause its neck to be cut, rather than by drawing it across the knife.
as will be explained. Below 3:11.
if it was a bird. Which is not heavy like an animal.

and moved the knife forward and did not bring it back. He cut with the knife in the direction away from himself and did not return it toward himself, and with this cut he completed his entire slaughter.
his slaughter is valid. And there is no concern that he pressed on the knife more than necessary.
and severed it. Cut the head completely off the neck.
the full width of two necks. The length of the knife is twice the width of the neck of the animal being slaughtered.
and if not, his slaughter is invalid. For it is clear that he applied great pressure on the knife, and this is not slaughter.
slaughter done like a quill. Diagonally, like a quill, which is a writing instrument made from a reed cut at a diagonal.
like a comb. The cut in the slaughter is serrated like a comb.
the slaughter of non-sacred animals does not require intent. Unlike the slaughter of sacred animals (Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashin 1:3).
like one acting without intent. Without intention.
who threw a knife to stick it in the wall. He intended only that it stick in the wall.
a deaf-mute, an imbecile or a minor. Who have no capacity for intent.
and others watch them that the slaughter is done properly. For otherwise there is concern that they will spoil the slaughter (below 4:5).

a wheel of stone or wood in which the knife was fixed, etc.. A machine that moves the knife and is operated by turning the wheel. And if water turns the wheel... it is invalid. Since the slaughter is not by human power.
released. Opened, allowed the water to flow out.
and slaughtered by its turning. By means of the turning of the wheel.
in the first turning. The first turn of the wheel after the stream of water reached it.
for the sake of mountains, for the sake of hills, etc.. In their honor.
for healing. Thinking that this act would help for healing.
nonsense. Meaningless words.
his slaughter is invalid. But the meat is permitted for benefit.
if he slaughtered for the sake of the constellation of the sea, etc.. The heavenly power appointed over that thing, and this is idolatry.
like any offering to idolatry. What was offered to idolatry, and it is forbidden for benefit (Hilchot Avodah Zarah 7:2).
for such a thought disqualifies them. Even though the thought is about an act that will be done later.

as will be explained in Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashin. 15:10. 16. Perhaps its end proved its beginning. Perhaps from what he intended at the end it is evident that also when he began to slaughter he intended it for idolatry.

for the sake of offerings that are brought as vows and freewill offerings, as well as their like. For the sake of those offerings that one can bring at any time at the offerer's wish (see Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 14:1).
like one who slaughters sacred offerings outside. Like one who slaughters offerings outside the Temple, whose slaughter is invalid.
they do not come as vow or freewill offering. Offerings that must be brought only in certain cases as obligations.
for the sake of an olah... a todah. Offerings that can be volunteered or vowed.
since the Pesach offering is set aside all year, etc.. And therefore, although it is an obligatory offering, it is included here among the offerings that come as a vow or freewill offering.
for the sake of a sin offering, etc.. Obligatory offerings that cannot be volunteered. 19. For the sake of the substitute for my offering. In place of the offering that is at home.
for he has substituted it. And its law is like that of a substitute offering, where both the first animal and its replacement are sacred (Leviticus 27:10).
perhaps she miscarried. In which case she has the law of a woman after childbirth regarding an offering (Hilchot Mechusrei Kapparah 1:6).
it has a voice. The matter becomes publicized.
the essence of naziriteship is a vow among vows. Since one can vow naziriteship at any time, it is included among the sacred items that come as a vow or freewill offering.
for the sake of something for which the slaughterer's slaughter is forbidden. For example, sacred offerings or idolatry.
they slaughtered one after the other. One began the slaughter and the second continued it.
a Jew does not forbid something that is not his. For further examples see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 8:1, Hilchot Kilayim 5:8 and others.
his intention was only to cause him distress. To distress the owner, and he did not really intend to consecrate it.
for we are concerned only with the thought of the slaughterer, etc.. That only the thoughts of the slaughterer himself are taken into account, and not those of the owners.
a gentile who slaughtered... even if he was a minor. Whose thought is not for idolatry.
as will be explained. Below 4:11.
they invalidate the slaughter. They disqualify it.
and these are shehiyah, chaladah, etc.. These terms will be explained in the course of the chapter.
shehiyah. Pausing and interruption in the middle of the slaughter.
and raised his hand. Raised the hand holding the knife.
and paused. Waited.
enough time to lift the animal, lay it down and slaughter. A measure of time sufficient to lift the animal off the ground, lay it down again and slaughter it.
if it was a small animal, etc.. A sheep or goat, and the measure of pause is measured by lifting and laying down a sheep or goat.
and if it was a large animal, etc.. Cattle; we measure by lifting and laying down cattle, which is a longer time.

and for a bird, enough time to lift a small animal, lay it down and slaughter. The majority of the two simanim, although in a bird there is no lifting and laying down at all, and its slaughter is of one siman; we use the pause measure for a small animal, which is the shorter one.
when you calculate, all the time of the pauses will combine, etc.. If one calculates and adds the pauses together, they combine to the measure of a pause.
and the time it takes to slaughter the minority of the simanim. Less than the majority of the windpipe and gullet.
the majority of one in a bird or the majority of two in an animal. The windpipe or the gullet, and this is the measure of their slaughter (above 1:9).
like one cutting the meat of a slaughtered animal. As if cutting the flesh of an animal that was already slaughtered, and it is not considered a pause in the slaughter itself.
he goes back and finishes the slaughter and it is nothing. There is no problem in this, since he cut a windpipe not through its majority, it is not significant.
that was cut.
was cut. Cut other than by valid slaughter.
as will be explained. Below halachah 19.
his slaughter has already been completed. Since a bird is made valid by slaughter of one siman.
he slaughtered the bird and paused in it. And did not finish cutting the majority of the windpipe.
and he does not know whether the gullet was punctured. And the bird became a neveilah (below halachah 19).
he goes back and slaughters the windpipe alone in another place. To ensure a complete slaughter, and afterward he can check the gullet.
he checks the gullet from the inside. Since the inner skin of the gullet is white and allows the check, while the outer skin is red; see below halachot 20-22.
it is known that it was not punctured. During the first slaughter, since a puncture would have caused bleeding in the gullet.
chaladah. Stabbing in the knife.

that the upper siman was cut upward. Upward, not in the usual manner of cutting. 10. If he buried the knife under tangled wool. That is, he did not clear the wool from the neck but thrust the knife under it, until it reached the animal's skin.

he slaughtered the minority of the simanim with chaladah and finished the slaughter without chaladah. He began to slaughter with chaladah the minority of the simanim (less than the majority), and slaughtered the rest of the simanim (the majority) validly (Kesef Mishneh, and see below halachah 13).
derasah. An act of chopping with force.
like one cutting a radish or a cucumber. Hard vegetables, which are cut by pressing the knife and not by drawing it.
hagramah. Deviation from the place of slaughter.
in a place not fit for slaughter. As detailed above 1:5-7.
two wheat-grain shapes. Bulges that resemble wheat kernels.
in the large ring. The windpipe is made of rings of cartilage. The large ring is the uppermost of them all and is located below the 'hat' (see above 1:7), and within it are the 'wheat grains.'
displaced. Slaughtered with the defect of hagramah.
he deviated at first by a third. Not necessarily a third, but less than half of the siman.
he deviated at first, etc.. That in any case where there is a majority not cut with deviation, it is valid.

and if he pressed... it is invalid. Unlike hagramah, derasah or chaladah invalidate even if done on the minority (see above halachah 10), but if they were in the last third they do not invalidate, since a valid slaughter of the majority of the simanim had already taken place.
ikkur. Uprooting the simanim from their place.
and one of them was dislodged. Came out of its place of attachment in the jaw.
his slaughter is valid. Since at the time of the uprooting the bird had already been made valid by slaughter.
it was dangling and would not be slaughtered. A loose siman would not be slaughtered.
as he commanded. As Moses was commanded in the Oral Torah (above 1:1).
as we explained. Above 1:13, Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 4:1.
lashes for rebellion. Rabbinic lashes.
whose thigh and its hollow were removed. That is missing from the animal. The hollow of the thigh is the flesh covering the pelvis.
so that it looks deficient when it lies down. When it lies on the ground the deficiency is noticeable.
if the spinal vertebrae were broken and most of the flesh with it. The neck vertebrae were broken, and the flesh on them was also severed.
it is a neveilah from life. Although the animal is alive, it is considered a complete neveilah (see Hilchot She'ar Avot HaTum'ah 2:1).
one that is not opposite the other is a neveilah. Since the skins move and the holes may lie one over the other.
the membrane is nothing. It is of no use.
a thorn was found standing in the gullet. Stuck in the wall of the gullet.

the thorn was found lengthwise in the gullet. That is, it is not stuck in the wall but lies inside it along the length of the gullet. 22. And the gullet has no check from the outside but only from the inside. Since the outer skin of the gullet is red and blood is not noticeable on it, but its inner skin is white and allows the check (above halachah 20).

that most of its cavity was severed. That it was cut through the majority of the circumference of its inner cavity. And we measure by the majority of the circumference of the cavity and not by the majority of the walls, since the thickness of the windpipe's walls is not uniform.
if it was punctured like an issar. If an area the size of the coin called an issar was missing from the wall.
holes in which there is no loss. There are many holes, but nothing was lost from the body of the windpipe itself.
a strip was removed from it. A long, narrow piece was lost.

whenever, if he folds the strip... and places them on the mouth of the windpipe. He imagines that he takes the strip that was removed, or combines the places that have holes into a single piece, and places them on the circumference of the windpipe's opening, and sees whether the missing parts cover the majority of the circumference.

a hole through both of its sides, enough for an issar to enter its width. A hole in both walls of the windpipe, one opposite the other; in this case we do not calculate the full area of the issar, but only that its width fit in each one.
it was split lengthwise... valid. Since a split along the length of the windpipe stays closed and pressed together and may heal thanks to the stretching of the neck.
they estimate. They compare.

from a large ring... from a small one. The windpipe is made of rings of cartilage ('large ring'), and between each one is connected soft tissue ('small ring'). 1. Five things. Derasah, shehiyah, chaladah, hagramah and ikkur (as detailed above 3:1-17).
and this is close to a doubtful neveilah. For there is a high chance that its slaughter was invalid and the animal became a neveilah.
proper and complete. For we see that the majority of the windpipe and the majority of the gullet were cut.
that he paused or pressed. Above 3:2, 3:11.
he slaughters with a nicked knife. Above 1:14.
and the like. Disqualifications that cannot be detected after the slaughter.
a deaf-mute. Who does not hear and does not speak (Hilchot Ishut 2:26).
and a minor. Before he has become thirteen years old and has shown signs of maturity (there 2:10).
they will spoil in their slaughter. They will slaughter improperly and make the animal a neveilah (see also below 12:4).
their slaughter is valid. Since intent for slaughter is not required, only a valid act (above 2:11-12).

who is not known to us. We do not know this person and his slaughtering ability. 7. For most of those present at slaughter are experts. The act of slaughter requires expertise, so one should assume that most of those engaged in it are expert slaughterers.
became a neveilah. Became a neveilah through invalid slaughter.
who became mute. Became unable to speak.
and his mind is sound. Sane and understanding.
one who does not hear. But who speaks.
he may slaughter. For he is not considered a deaf-mute.
a gentile who slaughtered. See also above 2:22. 12. And they made a great fence. A decree of the Sages whose purpose is to keep far from such a situation.
slaughter exists from beginning to end. Slaughter is a continuous act from its beginning to its end, and every stage of it is part of this sequence (see also Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashin 1:18).
who slaughtered half the windpipe. Half the trachea, since such a cut does not make the animal a neveilah (above 3:6-7).
a convert to apostasy for one of the transgressions. One who regularly and deliberately commits a certain transgression.
for his presumption is that he does not bother to check. Since he treats one commandment lightly, he likely treats this commandment lightly too.
one who publicly desecrates the Sabbath. In public, and he is considered as one who serves idolatry (Hilchot Shabbat 30:15).

as we explained in Hilchot Teshuvah. 3:7-8. And there he distinguished between the different types, defined the minim separately, those who deny the Torah separately, and one who denies Moses our teacher as a general category among the apikorsim.
disqualified from testimony, etc.. A person who commits transgressions for which one is liable to Torah lashes, and who is therefore disqualified from testifying (Hilchot Edut 10:3).
who does not leave a permitted thing. If he has the possibility of doing something permitted, he will not choose the path of prohibition (see also Hilchot Temurah 2:3).
a presumption about all Israel. See also Hilchot Edut 11:7.
the Sadducees and the Boethusians. Disciples of Zadok and Boethus, who believed only in the Written Torah and not in the tradition of the Sages.
they wring the neck. They kill other than by slaughter.
and this commandment. That one who wants to slaughter should not slaughter non-sacred animals but only peace offerings.
and they were commanded there. In the wilderness.
we have already explained in Hilchot Forbidden Foods. 4:6-9.
for the verse spoke of the common case. The verse gave an example from what is frequent.
and broke it. Wounded it.
and there are there. Are found.
diseases. Illnesses and wounds.
a law given to Moses at Sinai. A tradition of the Oral Torah.
and eight kinds of terefot were told to Moses at Sinai. And all seventy terefot enumerated below, 10:9, are included in these eight kinds.
mauled. Will be explained in this chapter.
punctured. Will be explained below, chapters 6-7.
missing, removed. Will be explained below, chapter 8.
severed. Will be explained below 9:1-4.
torn. Will be explained below 9:5-7.
fallen. Will be explained below 9:8-20.
and broken. Will be explained below 10:1-6.
although all of them are a law given to Moses at Sinai. And the status of all eight is equal in severity.
and any doubt that arises about mauling is forbidden. As will be explained below, halachah 11.
as will be explained. See below 9:7.
and it presses upon it with its hand. It sinks the claws of its front paw into it.
large. Big (in animals: cattle).
small. Small (in animals: sheep and goats).
and upward. And any animal larger than it.
to the body cavity. A place containing internal organs.
with the predator's hand. With its front leg.
with its legs. The hind ones.
mauled and was killed. The one that mauled.
we do not worry about it. And it needs no examination.
from the hip socket. From the hip joint.
the crown of the head. The head, including the brain.
opposite the intestines. The flesh in the area of the digestive system.
decayed. Rotted and crumbling.
that the physician scrapes off the wound. That has no hope of healing and must be removed. 10. In the simanim. Windpipe and gullet.
perhaps it rubbed against the wall. And a claw that was there became lodged in its back. Its anger subsided. It calmed down after it killed one of them, and we do not worry that it mauled the rest.
the reeds. Reed plants.
into its inner cavity. Into its internal cavity.
by even a tiny amount. In any amount at all.
the gullet's lining. The pharynx (its law will be explained below, halachah 2).
and the membrane of the brain of the head. Its law will be explained below, halachot 3-4.
and the heart with its windpipe. Its law will be explained below, halachah 5.
and the gall bladder. The gall sac (its law will be explained below, halachot 6-7).
and the liver tubes. The blood vessels in the liver (their law will be explained below, halachot 8-9).
and the abomasum, the rumen, the omasum and the reticulum. The four compartments of the stomach of ruminants (their law will be explained below, halachot 10-12).
and the small intestines. The intestines (their law will be explained below, halachot 13-16).
and the lung with its windpipe. The trachea (and its laws will be explained below, chapter 7).
we have already explained its measure. Above 1:6.
to the poles. Two protrusions at the back of the skull bone, to which the spine attaches and through which the spinal cord passes.
its membrane will have a different law. That it is not disqualified by a puncture (for its law see below 9:1).
poured out like water or like wax. It became liquid; wax is beeswax, which becomes a thick liquid when melted.

whether into the large cavity on the left or the small cavity on the right. For in Maimonides' view the heart has two cavities, and the large cavity is on the left side (Commentary on the Mishnah, Chullin 3:1).
and the heart's pipe. The pulmonary artery. Some explain it as the aorta (which leads toward the lung).
the conduit. A blood vessel.
a gall bladder that was punctured and the liver blocks it. The gall bladder is located next to the liver, and therefore a puncture in it can be blocked by the liver.
a kernel. A pit.
it is digested. It undergoes various processes.
when cutting the liver. When one cuts the liver.
and its sharp end was inward. Toward the inside of the liver, and its head toward the entrance of the large bronchus (see below halachah 9).
it is known that it punctured it as it entered. During its entry inward through the blood vessels it punctured them.
the round head. The blunt end of the needle.
it went through the bronchi. It passed through the blood vessels without puncturing them.
it is permitted. For in this place we do not suspect that it punctured.
liver flesh that became wormy. Eaten by worms, but the blood vessels remained intact.
and permitted fat blocks the puncture. For part of the fat around the stomach is forbidden as chelev, and part is permitted (for details see Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 7:6).
from the fat of the heart. The fat in the upper part of the heart.
and the sac on the heart. The membrane that wraps the heart.
the liver's diaphragm. The diaphragm.

the white place in its middle. The diaphragm is made of a white sheet of tendons surrounded by red muscles attached to the walls and assisting in the breathing process. The tendon sheet is hard and therefore does not block the puncture, but the muscles are soft and do block it.
the last intestine. The rectum (below halachah 16).
and the fat of a wild animal. Which is permitted to eat. 11. Rumen. The rumen.
to the outside. To the abdominal cavity.
one of them punctured into the cavity of its neighbor. The inner partitions between them were punctured.
in the thickness of the reticulum. The place where it has two layers of skin.
that he force-fed it. Fed it.
a kortov of chiltit. A resin extracted from the roots of the chiltit plant, which is sharp.
the hadar of the kanah. The large intestine, which is coiled around itself.
and moisture. Mucus stuck to the walls of the intestine.
and they are punctured. When he returned them, a puncture was found in them.
we attribute it to him. We assume that he punctured them.
and we compare. We match them up.
they arrange. They lay the intestines next to one another in order to compare.
that came out. Outside the body through a hole that does not make the animal terefah (as explained below 9:5-7).
they were turned over. Their order and position changed.
and it cannot live. It cannot survive.
that the dung. Excrement.
the roots of the thighs. Where the thighs join the body.
in the place attached to the thighs it is permitted. Since the thighs block the puncture.
the crop. A kind of sac at the bottom of a bird's gullet in which the food stays and softens.
and the gizzard. The part of a bird's stomach whose function is to grind the food (see the illustration above, p. 182).
that is stretched out with the gullet when the bird extends its neck. And it is considered a continuation of the gullet.
two sacs. Two layers.
permitted. Since the layers are firmly attached and cover one another.
like the structure of the tongue. Similar to the tongue, whose outer part is thin and inner part is thick.
created lacking. Without that organ from birth.
